notes:
Account background: Argyle Threadsmith runs a mid-market ecommerce platform (marketplace + direct sellers). High ticket volume during promos (BFCM, promo weekends). They operate Zendesk and are piloting Freshdesk in EU region. Primary goal: reduce avg handle time and speed triage for agents via concise ticket/email summaries and reliable auto-tagging to wire into macros/flows.

Customer constraints / asks:
- Integrate with Zendesk macros + Freshdesk workflows: ability to return tags + suggested macro id. Tool-calling capability required: Redwood must be able to return a structured macro trigger so frontend can execute.
- P95 latency target for agent-facing summaries: <= 500ms (ideal <= 300ms) under normal load; must degrade gracefully under spikes.
- Throughput: baseline 100 req/s for live agent assist, burst to 500 req/s during promos.
- Cost sensitive: prefer open/quantized models for bulk summarization and embeddings for search/rerank.
- Security: SOC2 required, SSO/SAML, per-token audit logs, key management (KMS), and US data residency for primary dataset. Retention controls for transcripts (30/90/365 day policies).
- Accuracy/quality: Tag precision target >85%, summary usefulness >4/5 in agent feedback. Must not hallucinate order numbers or substitution-sensitive fields (quote: "If it invents order IDs we fail the pilot").

POC plan (proposed): 4 weeks
- Week 1: sample data ingest (Zendesk export), wire Zendesk webhook -> Redwood hosted endpoint (VPC connector), baseline latency/cost metrics
- Week 2: model selection + quantization tests; set up embeddings index for subject classification + reranking
- Week 3: live A/B with 10 agents (summaries + auto-tags applied as suggestions); collect precision/recall and agent satisfaction
- Week 4: finalize SLOs, security checklist, and recommend Dedicated sizing or Hosted+VPC config; deliver POC report

POC success criteria: tag precision >= 85%, summary conciseness score >= 4/5 (agent feedback), p95 latency <= 500ms, cost per ticket <= $0.12 (target).

Notes from calls / quotes:
- Lina (Head of CX): "We need summaries that are short, accurate, and never invent order numbers. If it reduces AHT by 20% we'll pay attention."
- Engineering: wants to evaluate both Hosted API with VPC peering and Redwood Dedicated for guaranteed capacity. Also asked about on-prem option for EU legal flows.
- Security team: asked for KMS integration diagram, audit log retention guarantees, and SOC2 + ISO mention.

Technical preferences: prefer open LLaMA-style variants for cost but will accept Redwood-verified models for critical flows. Interested in Redwood Optimize recommendations for batching + quantization.

Current commercial posture: Pricing deck reviewed (drive://Redwood/pricing/argyle-deck.pdf). Customer expects a mid-market committed ARR (est 50k-150k) if POC meets SLA and security checks. Procurement timeline: forecast 2026-04.

Next steps / owner actions:
- Redwood AE (Lena): send updated POC SOW and pricing by 2026-03-12 (missed; follow up 2026-03-11).
- SE (Ravi): schedule security deep-dive and provide KMS/HSM architecture.
- Infra: provide Dedicated sizing estimate and burst capacity numbers.

Blockers: security review still open; legal needs a data residency clause for EU customers; final SLA negotiation on p95 latency and uptime.
